title: Access fabric: role-graph and permissions grid for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: RBAC v1 has grown inconsistent across product surfaces (Console, API, Private installs). We need a single, explainable role model that supports multi-tenant hierarchies, fine-grained scopes (resource- and attribute-level), and operational admin controls while producing high-fidelity audit trails for compliance.

This ticket specifies the 'access fabric' approach: a directed role-graph (roles as nodes, inheritance and delegation as edges) orthogonal to a resource-type hierarchy (organization -> projects -> model-pools -> deployments -> secret-objects). Scopes are first-class constraints (resourcePath prefixes, label selectors, attribute predicates). A permissions grid maps atomic actions (read, write, manage, deploy, impersonate, billing) to resource types; effective permission evaluation is the intersection of granted scopes with request context, resolved via deterministic graph traversal and scope-merging rules.

Goals:
- Single canonical role-graph data model for all deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Deterministic allow/deny evaluation with clear precedence (deny > allow, explicit exceeds inherited).
- Rich audit events that capture both decision input (principal, assertion, scope) and decision rationale (path of role edges used).
- SSO/SAML + SCIM mapping guidance for automated provisioning and attribute-based scoping.
- Admin tooling: role simulation, emergency revoke, and delegated admin with boundaries.
decisions: Adopt default-deny semantics: no implicit allows, explicit grant required.
Role-graph nodes will be immutable versions; edits produce new node versions to enable clean rollbacks and diffing in audit logs.
Scope language: use a small predicate DSL supporting path-prefix, label-match, and attribute-equals (example: project:acme/* AND label:env=prod).
Permission primitives will be action-centric (generate_token, read_model, execute_inference, manage_billing) rather than broad verbs per resource.
Deny rules take precedence over allows. Explicit role bindings at a narrower scope override broader inherited allows only when explicit deny is absent.
Evaluation engine must return explanation metadata (role_ids, scope_intersection, final_decision) to be persisted in audit events for traceability.
Session-scoped temporary grants supported via time-bounded bindings and one-time breakglass tokens issued by audited workflows.
progress_updates: 2025-03-06: Kickoff workshop with Security, Platform, and Console teams. Collected common failure modes from customer-facing incidents (outage due to overly broad admin role).
2025-03-09: Drafted resource-type taxonomy and atomic action list; validated against three representative customer setups (single-tenant SaaS, multi-tenant orgs, on-prem air-gapped).

2025-03-11: PoC evaluator implemented (Python) that accepts role-graph + bindings + request context and returns decision + explanation. Performance baseline measured: avg 1.6ms per evaluation in microbench harness with 100 role nodes.
2025-03-14: Design review with Product and Legal. Legal requested retention and export formats for audit logs (see audit notes).
2025-03-18: Incorporated reviewer feedback; preparing schema PR and console simulation UI wireframes.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical role-graph schema merged to platform repo and documented in Confluence.
Permission primitives and resource taxonomy approved by Product and Security.
Evaluator library released with unit tests and performance benchmarks (<= 3ms median on typical role sets).
Audit events include decision_explanation and are persisted to the platform audit stream with exportable JSON option.
SCIM/SSO mapping doc and sample SAML assertion templates published; provisioning flow validated in staging.
Console role-simulator MVP implemented and accessible to org admins behind flag.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Read-only pilot — import existing RBAC v1 role bindings into v2 model with a 'compat' layer that evaluates both models and emits diffs. Phase 2: Soft-enforcement — surface missing explicit grants in admin console and gate risky operations behind warnings. Phase 3: Opt-in enforcement per org with telemetry. Phase 4: Full-enforce after 90-day opt-in window; provide rollback via role-graph versioning and audit snapshots.
audit_logging_considerations: Audit schema must include: event_id, timestamp, principal_id, role_graph_snapshot_id, evaluated_role_ids, requested_action, target_resource_path, scope_match_details (list of matched scopes as text), final_decision, decision_rationale (short text), request_context (ip, session_id, assertion_attributes), and supporting_pr (if change originated from UI or infra PR). Logs forwarded to central audit pipeline (Kafka -> long-term cold storage). Retention: 1 year hot, 7 years cold for enterprise customers. Access controls: only Security/Compliance and delegated auditors can query raw audit logs; console will present redacted views for admins.
sso_saml_notes: SCIM will map IdP groups to role bindings by externalId. SAML assertions may include attributes that constrain bindings at session time (e.g., assertion.project=acme -> create scoped binding on-the-fly). Recommend scanning IdP group names and attributes during provisioning to suggest least-privilege mappings. Document example SAML attribute statements for Okta and Azure AD and include a validator to test attribute-based scoping in staging.
admin_controls:
- Breakglass: time-limited emergency token flow that requires multi-party approval and emits high-priority audit events.
- Delegated admins: support 'scoped-admin' roles (e.g., billing-admin@org/project) with explicit non-transitive bindings.
- Simulation UI: run a hypothetical request against live role-graph and show which bindings were considered.
- Revoke/rotation: provide bulk revoke by role or by principal and immediate soft-failover to read-only if necessary.
- Alerts: generate immediate Alert channel events when an admin binding is created with global scope.
reviewer_feedback: Mateo Sanchez (Product): requested clearer semantics for billing vs. org-management actions and examples for delegations.
Tara O'Neill (Legal): asked for exportable CSV schema and record-of-access report for compliance audits.
Danielle Moore (Security): suggested adding signed integrity checks on role-graph snapshots persisted to S3 and restricting rollback to authorized service principals.
UX (Luca Marino): recommends simulation output include a human-readable decision tree and not just role IDs.
